how_to_read_for_egret: raw_records and findings are EVIDENCE of what Kestra did with the three plugins. egret_expected holds typed values later tasks deserialize; each carries `basis`: measured (on the artifact), code (javap of the jars), schema (the plugin API's JSON schema or description, not run), or chosen/unmeasured. Log messages longer than 700 chars (stack traces) are truncated in the fixture and marked; no finding quotes a truncated part.

findings.finding: The three Maven Central 2.0.0 jars are byte-identical to the jars the pinned image already ships in /app/plugins (io_kestra_plugin__plugin-jdbc-{postgres,trino,mysql}__2_0_0.jar): same sha256 (raw_records.image_plugin_jars_sha256). The image bundles 205 plugin jars; GET /api/v1/plugins therefore lists each of the three groups twice (bundled + mounted), both at version 2.0.0. The artifact did not refuse the jars.

GET /api/v1/plugins lists these task classes: postgres Batch, CopyIn, CopyOut, Queries, Query; trino Query; mysql Batch, Queries, Query; plus one Trigger per plugin (out of scope, spec §11). Schemas were read from GET /api/v1/plugins/<FQCN>?all=true (without all=true the base-task properties id/type/timeout/retry/... are omitted).

With no fetchType, Query on all three plugins produced the same outputs as fetchType: NONE, an empty object `{}` (no `size` key). The schema agrees: `"default": "NONE"` on Query and Queries (Trigger defaults to FETCH).

FETCH_ONE -> `{"row": {...}, "size": 1}`; FETCH -> `{"rows": [...], "size": 2}`; STORE -> `{"uri": "kestra:///w5b/<flow-id-with-dashes>/executions/<id>/tasks/q/<taskrun>/<n>.ion", "size": 2}`; NONE -> `{}`. Queries (postgres) FETCH -> `{"outputs": [{"rows": [...], "size": 1}, ...]}` one entry per statement; Queries STORE -> one kestra:// uri per statement.

Rendered values, identical across Postgres, Trino and StarRocks where the type exists: integer `1`; text `"a"`; DECIMAL(10,2) 12.34 -> `12.34` and 0.10 -> `0.1` (a JSON number, trailing zero lost); TIMESTAMP -> `"2026-01-02T03:04:05.123456"` and `"2026-12-31T23:59:59"` (ISO, no zone, fraction only when non-zero); TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-01-02 03:04:05+07' -> `"2026-01-01T20:04:05.000000Z"` (UTC, always 6 digits; Postgres and Trino); DATE -> `"2026-01-02"`; boolean -> `true` (StarRocks `true` too); BIGINT 9007199254740993 -> `9007199254740993` (exact); DOUBLE 1.5 -> `1.5`. **A NULL column is absent from the row object**: row 1 has no `n` key, row 2 has `"n": 7`.
A successful Query writes exactly one execution log line, level DEBUG: `Starting query: <sql>` (the rendered SQL). No INFO line. Asking the logs API with minLevel=TRACE returned the same count (1).

A failing Query (bad SQL) ends task and execution FAILED. Postgres: DEBUG `Starting query: SELEC 1`, ERROR `ERROR: syntax error at or near "SELEC"\n  Position: 1` (the exception message), DEBUG `org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: ...` (the stack trace). Trino adds a second ERROR line (`line 1:1: mismatched input 'SELEC'. ...\nnull`) after `Query failed (#<query id>): line 1:1: ...`. StarRocks via mysql: ERROR `Getting syntax error at line 1, column 0. Detail message: Unexpected input 'SELEC', ...`. The task run carries no message field: the reason exists only in the log lines.

`password: "{{ secret('PGPASS') }}"` with SECRET_PGPASS=base64(w5bSecretPw42) authenticated to Postgres (every pg run SUCCESS); the control with a wrong literal password FAILED with `FATAL: password authentication failed for user "w5b"`. A missing secret fails the task: ERROR `io.pebbletemplates.pebble.error.PebbleException: Cannot find secret for key 'NOPE'. ({{ secret('NOPE') }}:1)`.

The plugin never logs the URL or the password. A secret inside the SQL is masked in the log line: `Starting query: SELECT '******' AS leaked`; an error echoing it verbatim is masked: `ERROR: relation "******" does not exist`. The **output is not masked**: the row is `{"leaked": "w5bSecretPw42"}`. An echo the engine re-encoded is not masked: with the unquoted identifier Postgres folds case and the ERROR line reads `ERROR: relation "w5bsecretpw42" does not exist` (the SQL line itself is masked: `SELECT * FROM ******`).

POST /flows with a top-level `pluginDefaults` returns 422 `Validation failed`, detail `Unrecognized field "pluginDefaults" (class io.kestra.core.models.flows.FlowWithSource), not marked as ignorable (26 known properties: ...)`. Same response for a list with a plugin task, `pluginDefaults: []` on a flow with only a Log task, and a list on a Log-only flow. POST /flows/validate returns 200 with `constraints: "Validation error: Unrecognized field \"pluginDefaults\" ..."`. The refusal comes from the JSON deserializer (unknown field), not from a dedicated FlowService message.

With `timeout: PT5S`, Kestra ends the task only when `run()` returns. Postgres `SELECT pg_sleep(600)`: the task stayed RUNNING, execution duration PT10M0.50705S, then FAILED with ERROR `Timeout after 00:00:05.000`; pg_stat_activity listed backend 133 `active` on `SELECT pg_sleep(600)` at run start +15 s (10 s after the timeout was due), +60 s and +300 s, and `idle` only at the terminal probe. ERR` at +300 s: the query was ended by StarRocks's own `query_timeout` (300, raw_records.starrocks_query_timeout), not by Kestra. Trino: FAILED after PT5.134766S, the query `FAILED ... USER_CANCELED` in system.runtime.queries, end 02:04:16.320 (the thread interrupt reaches Trino's HTTP client).

findings.finding: Kestra's explicit kill (DELETE /executions/<id>/actions/kill -> WorkerTaskCallable.kill: task.kill(), then a thread interrupt). Postgres: the query went `idle` within 1 s, the task logged ERROR `ERROR: canceling statement due to user request`, execution **FAILED** (not KILLED) 0.52 s after the request. Trino: execution KILLED 0.53 s after the request, query `USER_CANCELED`. StarRocks: **the kill did not end the query**: `SELECT SLEEP(120)` ran to completion and the execution ended **SUCCESS** 116.34 s after the kill request (4 s + 116 s = the full 120 s); with connectionPooling: false, SHOW PROCESSLIST at kill +10 s showed connection 33554516 with Command `Query`, Time `15`, Info `SELECT SLEEP(90)` and the execution ended SUCCESS 86.28 s after the kill.
findings.raw: raw_records.runs.pg_killapi_alone, trino_killapi, sr_killapi_alone, sr_killapi_nopool (engine_probes, kill, logs)

findings.finding: The StarRocks kill blocks the caller until the query ends. Measured: with a StarRocks kill and a Postgres kill requested 0.04 s apart, the worker logged `Killing running task` for the StarRocks task only; the Postgres `Received kill command` came at 02:13:08, when StarRocks's query_timeout ended its query, and pid 167's `SELECT pg_sleep(601)` was `active` at 02:13:03 and `idle` at 02:13:07 (raw_records.watch_after_sr_kill, kestra_kill_log_lines). Code: `AbstractJdbcBaseQuery.kill(Statement)` calls `Statement.isClosed()` before `cancel()` (javap), and the bundled MySQL Connector/J 26.7.0 `StatementImpl.isClosed()` takes the connection lock (`getConnectionLock` + `Lock.lock`) that `executeInternal` holds while the query runs. So `cancel()` is never reached while the query runs.

In all three 2.0.0 jars `AbstractJdbcQuery` has `public void kill()` which calls `AbstractJdbcBaseQuery.kill(Statement)` (isClosed, cancel, close) then `kill(Connection)` (isClosed, close). `runningStatement` is assigned before `execute` (bytecode offsets 202 and 320).

`connectionPooling` defaults to true (schema) and is in effect: the Postgres kill run reused backend pid 133 whose backend_start (02:04:06) predates the task (02:14:59). A per-attempt JVM has no pool to reuse; egret may leave the property as is.
io.kestra.plugin.jdbc.mysql.Query reaches StarRocks 4.1.4 with `url: jdbc:mysql://starrocks:9030/`, `username: root`, no password: every sr_fetch_* run SUCCESS with rows.

Measured to write internal storage (a kestra:// uri in outputs): `fetchType: STORE` on Query (all three) and on Queries (postgres); deprecated `store: true` on postgres Query; the whole `CopyOut` class (`{"uri": "kestra:///.../copy-out", "rowCount": 1}`). Schema-described (basis schema, not run): `Batch.from` and `CopyIn.from` are required kestra:// URIs ("Input file from internal storage"), `mysql.Query/Queries.inputFile` is a kestra:// URI. `outputFiles: [out]` on postgres Query ran SUCCESS with no uri in outputs; its description says only embedded drivers support it.
